title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 21 (Commencement of arbitral proceedings)

content.overview: Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, arbitral proceedings in respect of a particular dispute commence on the date on which a request for that dispute to be referred to arbitration is received by the respondent.
content.glance: Commencement = receipt of request to refer the dispute to arbitration, unless the parties agree otherwise.
content.study: Default commencement is receipt by the respondent of the request to refer the dispute to arbitration. The parties may agree otherwise. The date matters for limitation and procedural sequencing; proof of receipt may engage section 3.

sections.heading: Default rule
sections.body: Commencement on the date the respondent receives the request to refer the dispute to arbitration.

sections.heading: Party agreement
sections.body: The parties may agree on a different commencement rule.

sections.heading: Dispute-specific
sections.body: Commencement is assessed in respect of the particular dispute referred.

misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.
